0|411486626e5779bd85439282985ff3fc25a3f6d2|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"bpf/xdp: optimize bpf_xdp_pointer to avoid reading sinfo
Currently we observed a significant performance degradation in
samples/bpf xdp1 and xdp2
added in commit 772251742262 (""samples/bpf: fixup some tools to be able
to support xdp multibuffer"").
This patch reduce the overhead by avoiding to read/load shared_info
(sinfo) memory area
column2: when XDP packet don't have any frags. This improves

column1: performance because sinfo is located in another cacheline.
Function bpf_xdp_pointer() is used by BPF helpers bpf_xdp_load_bytes()
and bpf_xdp_store_bytes(). As a help to reviewers
potentially access sinfo
column2: but it uses xdp_buff_has_frags() flags bit check

column1: to avoid accessing sinfo in no-frags case.
The likely/unlikely instrumentation lays out asm code such that sinfo
access isn't interleaved with no-frags case (checked on GCC 12.2.1-4).
The generated asm code is more compact towards the no-frags case.
The BPF kfunc bpf_dynptr_slice() also use bpf_xdp_pointer(). Thus
should also take effect for that.
